chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah, so he said: Go to Abd al-Malik ibn Jurayj and ask him about it, for he has knowledge of it. I met him and he dictated to me a great deal regarding its permissibility. Among what Ibn Jurayj narrated to me was: 'There is no fixed time limit nor a limit in number [of wives] for it; it is in the status of slave girls. A man marries from them as he wishes, and the owner of four wives may marry as many as he wishes without a guardian or witnesses. When the period expires, she departs from him without divorce, and he gives her a small amount [as dowry]. Her waiting period is two menstrual cycles, and if she does not menstruate, then forty-five days.' I brought the book to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and presented it to him, so he said: He is truthful and confirmed it.

key_terms.ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ: Abd al-Malik ibn Jurayj, a key narrator whose report was confirmed
key_terms.الْإِمَاء: Slave girls (used here as a comparative legal status)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and rulings for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Ibn Jurayj and authenticated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), provides a detailed jurisprudential framework for Mut'ah, emphasizing its flexibility by noting the absence of fixed duration or numerical limits on partners. It highlights key legal distinctions from permanent marriage, such as the lack of requirement for a guardian (wali) or witnesses, and specifies that the contract terminates automatically upon the agreed term's expiry without the need for formal divorce (talaq). This narration serves as a primary evidence in Shia jurisprudence for the validity and specific conditions of temporary marriage.

en.ammaar-muslim: 8. [8/-] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar b. Udhayna from Ismail b. al-Fadhl al-Hashimi who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about Mut’a so he said: go and see Abd al-Malik b. Jurayj and ask him about it for he has some knowledge about it, so I met him and he (Ibn Jurayj) dictated a lot of material in regards its permissibility to me, so from among that which Ibn Jurayj transmitted to me included: it (Mut’ah) has no fixed duration nor limit in number [of partners with whom you can contract], it has the same status as [union with] slave girls, a man marries with them as he likes, even someone who already has four wives can marry as many as he wishes, without [permission from] guardian required nor witnesses, so when the period terminates she departs from him without divorce, and he gives her some small thing [as her Mahr], and her Idda is two menstrual cycles, and if she does not menstruate then forty five days, so I came with the book to Aba Abdillah عليه السلام and presented its contents to him, so he said: he is truthful, and he agreed with it.
